children: Novo Nordisk
is eyeing the hair-loss market as the Ozempic maker
looks to diversify as part of its post-Wegovy growth strategy, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday following an interview with its top executives.
“We could leverage our scientific knowledge potentially moving into that space,” Novo’s
Chief Scientific Officer Martin Lange said, adding, “It’s not necessarily what we’ll pursue first, but that would be a clear possibility.”
Hair-loss drug developers Veradermics
and Absci
traded higher after the remarks that came a day after Novo
laid out its post-Wegovy growth strategy amid an increasingly crowded GLP-1 market.

Shares of the Danish drugmaker fell on Monday even as its long-term goals indicated plans to launch more than five drugs with “multi-blockbuster” potential by 2030 and generate over $23B in risk-adjusted

“Confidence is gone, as shown yesterday by the reaction, and it takes time and hard work to build that back,” CEO Mike Doustdar said, adding, “We need to start somewhere, and then we need to search everywhere.”
Despite its first-mover advantage, Novo
has lost out to its main rival, Lilly
, in the injectable GLP-1 market, and a looming patent cliff beyond 2030 threatens its best-selling drug, semaglutide, marketed as Ozempic and Wegovy, for diabetes and weight loss, respectively.

According to Doustar, the company wants to target areas where its expertise in direct-to-consumer sales, increasingly used in selling its blockbuster weight loss drugs, can provide it with a chance “to win.”
Lange said that given their shorter development timelines, some of the consumer-facing programs Novo
is evaluating could launch by the end of the decade, and the company could also sign deals for late-stage compounds.

Since the 1990s, there have been no FDA-approved therapies for pattern hair loss, which affects an estimated 50M men and 30M women in the U.S. However, hair loss is not among the eight conditions for which Novo
is planning to run mid-stage trials by later this year or early next year.

The company has said it will seek bolt-on deals and leverage its internal drug pipeline more quickly, as it intends to advance new treatments for conditions including heart, liver, and blood disorders. Cardiology programs would have longer timelines, Lange said.

title: Novo eyes hair-loss market as Ozempic maker looks to diversify
